races.title: State House, District 25
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Allen Chesser
cands.bio: Republican who represented North Carolina House District 25 (part of Nash County) from 2023. Army National Guard veteran (2003-2009) who deployed to Iraq, and a former police officer in Nags Head and Raleigh. Lost the 2018 Republican primary for Congress.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Chesser was born, where he grew up, or when he came to or lived in specific parts of North Carolina beyond his school, police and Nash County residence. We found no documented positions from him on data centers or on new development. We found no controversies, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, and the sources contain no 2026 platform beyond his campaign site. His statements about bills he voted for or sponsored come only from his own campaign site and were not independently confirmed. We found nothing on his positions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B visas, or campaign-money pledges.

local.label: Roots 90: He graduated from Bunn High School in 2003 and enlisted in the military at 17. He later worked as a police officer in Nags Head and Raleigh and now lives in the Samaria community of Nash County; his birthplace is not stated in the sources.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since January 2023, with a law enforcement career as a police officer in Nags Head and Raleigh and Army National Guard service from 2003 to 2009, including an Iraq deployment.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service, which counts toward the high range. His career background is law enforcement rather than law, policy or budget work, so he is scored below the top of the range.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service, which counts toward the high range. His career background is law enforcement rather than law, policy or budget work, so he is scored below the top of the range.

pro-life.evidence: Said in his 2022 Ballotpedia survey that he would put his full and total support behind the Life at Conception Act.

second-amendment.evidence: Said in his 2022 Ballotpedia survey that he would fight to expand Second Amendment rights by defending Constitutional Carry and opposing anyone in Raleigh who wants to disarm North Carolinians.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to expand access to charter schools and supports families deciding what education is best for their children. This is his own claim and was not checked against a legislative record.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he sponsored and voted for bills raising penalties for rioting, assaulting law enforcement officers and firing weapons at emergency vehicles, and that he secured $5 million for the Nash County Sheriff's detention center. This is his own claim and was not checked against a legislative record.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

cands.name: Lorenza M. Wilkins
cands.bio: Nonprofit executive and Nash County resident of over 27 years. Past roles include Executive Director at Rebound: Alternatives for Youth, Senior Director at Made in Durham, FUSE Corps Executive Fellow and CSX Talent Advisor. Co-founded Compass Youth Center. Lost the 2024 House District 25 race. No prior elected office.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists recommendations from Sway voting groups, including 92% Club, Bull City Anna's Voting Group, Imani's Pix, Unburdening The Ballot, Waves of Democracy and YALLvote. These are voter-guide groups, not organizations.

cands.gaps: He has held no elected office, so there is no voting record or record of official actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or a pledge on donors. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his survey answers come from 2024. The pages we read do not say what year he moved to Nash County or give details of his childhood beyond his hometown and high school.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Roanoke Rapids, NC and his high school as Warren County High School, his campaign site calls him a native of Lake Gaston, NC, and he says he has lived in Nash County for over 27 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Over 20 years in private, public and nonprofit work: Talent Advisor at CSX, Program Manager at Triangle Literacy Council, Senior Director of Programs and Operations at Made in Durham, Executive Director at Rebound: Alternatives for Youth, FUSE Corps Executive Fellow, human resources leadership roles, and a nonprofit executive role (Chief Officer of People and Culture at Inter-Faith Food Shuttle per his 2024 Ballotpedia survey).
qual.why: He has management and executive experience in nonprofits and human resources, which fits the middle band. No legislative or other elected office is documented, and board and council seats are not counted.
qual.label: He has management and executive experience in nonprofits and human resources, which fits the middle band. No legislative or other elected office is documented, and board and council seats are not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign platform criticizes the General Assembly for taking money from public schools to fund private school vouchers, saying private school choice should not come at the expense of public schools. It also says teachers are leaving the state for better pay.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he listed 'Protecting Women's Reproductive Freedoms' among the policy areas he is passionate about.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 0 only promised
